title: Operational signal taxonomy and latency-correlations runbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc sketches an operational taxonomy for signals that matter when diagnosing latency-correlated incidents in the inference stack, plus pragmatic dashboard and tracing guidance for oncall and SREs. Goal is to reduce mean time to root cause (MTTR) for heavy-tail latency and correlated degradations across cache/batching/serving layers.

Audience:
- Oncall SREs and backend engineers
- Observability platform owners
- Product owners for Hosted/Dedicated/Private runtime features

High-level problem statement:
We see frequent incidents where 95th/99th latency spikes are correlated with: cache churn, KV cache eviction storms, batching perturbations, model swap fallbacks, and noisy upstream client behavior (long prefix sequences). Current dashboards scatter relevant signals across multiple pages and tracing sampling is too low for rare but high-impact spans. This doc proposes a compact signal taxonomy, prioritized widgets, and tracing adjustments to make triage faster.

Signal taxonomy (operational categories):
1) Client surface signals
   - request.size_bytes (histogram)
   - request.prompt_tokens (summary)
   - request.client_id (tagged counter for noisy clients)
2) Serving runtime signals
   - inference.latency_ms (histogram, per-model, per-hardware)
   - kvcache.hit_rate / kvcache.eviction_rate (ratio + event counter)
   - batch.size_distribution (histogram)
   - kernel_queue.depth (gauge per-GPU)
3) Scheduling & routing signals
   - route.fallback.count (count of requests rerouted to slower model variants)
   - autoscaler.burst_events (count + last_event_ts)
4) Resource contended signals
   - gpu.utilization (per-device)
   - mem.swap_events (host-level)
5) System topology & config churn
   - model.rollout.stage (tag: canary|prod|fallback)
   - infra.config_reloads (count of reload events)

Signal prioritization guidance:
- First-line signals for pager: per-model 95th latency (sustained > 2x baseline for 5m), kvcache.eviction_rate spike (> 10x baseline), batch.size median drop (> 50% of usual), route.fallback.count surge.
- Second-line (investigate if first-line positive): gpu.utilization anomalies, kernel_queue.depth backlog, mem.swap_events.
- Tertiary signals: config reloads, model rollout changes, client noise patterns.

Dashboard layout recommendations (single-page incident triage view):
Top row (health): tiny KPI chips for global 95th/99th, error rate, total req/s, active model variants.
Middle row (causal candidates):
 - latency histogram heatmap (per-model x token_bucket) showing hot rectangles for large prompts
 - kvcache heatmap: hit-rate over time + eviction spikes annotated with rollout windows
 - batch-size violin plots across serving nodes (detects splitting/under-batching)
Bottom row (drill anchors):
 - trace-sampler funnel control (current sampling rate, last sampled trace id)
 - recent config change timeline (links to rollouts)
Widget notes and heuristics:
- Heatmap bins: token length buckets (0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024) on X, latency percentile on Y. Use exponential color scaling to highlight rare but high-latency slices.
- Annotate traces in the heatmap with small icons when a trace exists for that time range to avoid blind spots.
- Use per-customer rate-limiting counters as an early warning chip; noisy clients often precede cache churn.

Tracing and sampling strategy (practical):
- Base sample rate: 0.5% of requests globally for full traces (default).
- Targeted uplift rules (on top of base):
  * If kvcache.eviction_rate > 5x baseline AND inference.latency_95 > baseline*1.5 -> sample 100% of requests for 10 minutes for affected model shard (auto-triggered).
  * If batch.size_median decreases below 50% normal -> sample 50% for 20 minutes for that route.
  * If route.fallback.count increases -> sample 100% of fallback flows (because fallback often loses KV context).
- Span instrumentation anchors: prefer adding small, constant-cost spans at
  * kv-cache.lookup (include hit/miss boolean)
  * batching.window.wait_ms
  * kernel.invoke (gpu id, queue depth metric tag)
  * model.variant.resolve (variant id)
- Trace size budget: cap span payloads; avoid logging full prompt content in spans — use prompt token count and hashed prompt id.

Runbook snippets (step-by-step)
1) Pager fires for high 95th latency on model X: quick checklist
   - Open incident triage view (single-page). Check small KPI chips.
   - Look at token-length vs latency heatmap: are hot rectangles concentrated in >256 token bucket? If yes, suspect client workload change.
   - Check kvcache.eviction_rate and kvcache.hit_rate: if eviction spike correlates, snapshot recent evictions (last 10m) and copy sample client IDs.
   - If eviction spike present: escalate to runtime team, enable temporary cache size increases (if policy allows) or rollback recent rollout.
2) If batch size collapse observed:
   - Verify autoscaler/burst_events and kernel_queue.depth for mismatches.
   - Check for upstream traffic shaping causing many small requests; contact client owner.
3) If nothing obvious in metrics:
   - Increase trace sampling via the uplift rules and collect full traces for 30 minutes. Look for long spans in kernel.invoke or serialization steps.

Operational playbooks for common root causes (short):
- KV eviction storms: identify noisy client(s) -> throttle via per-client token bucket -> add client to high-cold-cache list -> review cache TTL policy -> consider tiered cache (hot key pinning).
- Model fallback oscillation: detect route.fallback.count pulses -> stabilize by adding exponential backoff to fallback policy and enabling sticky routing for N minutes.
- Autoscaler thrash: observed as repeated autoscaler.burst_events -> increase cooldown window and add hysteresis on scaling decisions.

Cost and privacy considerations:
- Trace uplift will increase data volume and retention costs; limit full-trace retention to 7 days for uplifted windows and sample aggressively for historical storage.
- Avoid storing raw prompts in traces; use hashed ids and token counts. For customer debugging, require secure upload with consent and audit trail.

Open questions / TODOs:
- SDK hooks: need a low-overhead signal to mark long-prefix requests at client side for better correlation. (Action: eng-dx to prototype by 2025-03-01)
- Automated remediation: should we auto-increase cache size when eviction spike detected? Need risk review.
- Dashboard UX: add small inline links from widget to relevant PR/rollout when config changes match anomaly.

References and related artifacts:
- Linked Jira ticket OBS-412 has initial alert thresholds and pager schedule
- Telemetry config PR #88 contains the proposed uplift rules and sampling knobs
- Confluence page (Latency Incidents Taxonomy) holds historical incident notes and postmortems

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Might be worth a compact "triage URL" generator that pre-fills dashboard time-range and auto-tags the incident with the top-3 signal suspects.
- Consider a lightweight SLO slice per token-length bucket; allows more targeted paging for long-prefix workloads.

Sign-off checklist before moving to in_review:
- [ ] Confirm sampling uplift code merged and tested in staging
- [ ] Create incident dashboard template and add to runbooks library
- [ ] Run 2 tabletop drills with oncall to validate steps

Last notes:
This is a working draft. Expect frequent updates as we validate uplift rules in staging and get feedback from oncall rotations. If you want to help, drop a comment in the linked Slack thread or ping me (Asha).
